lead: Powder bed fusion (PBF) is an additive manufacturing family that spreads a thin layer of powder and fuses only the chosen cross-section with a laser or electron beam. Unfused powder stays in place and supports the next layer, so overhangs need no separate support structure. SLS fuses polymer powder by partial melting; SLM and DMLS fully melt metal powder. PBF makes complex brackets, dental crowns, implants and small production batches where tooling cost would dominate. This chapter follows the layer cycle and the main process variants.
prereq: You need: Chapter 7.2 for the AM process chain, and Unit 2, Powder metallurgy sintering, for particle bonding.

blocks.text: A powder bed fusion machine has a powder supply, a recoater blade or roller, a build platform and a focused energy beam. The platform starts below the powder bed top. The recoater spreads a fresh blanket of powder. The beam scans the CAD slice. Scanned powder fuses; loose powder stays around the part.

items: Lower the build platform by one layer thickness, for example 0.05 mm.
Raise powder from the supply or push it from a hopper.
Spread powder with the recoater at constant speed.
Scan the cross-section with the laser or electron beam.
Fuse particles by sintering or melting.
Lower the platform and repeat until all slices are built.
Remove the part and recycle or discard loose powder.

blocks.text: L<sub>layer</sub> = A<sub>layer</sub> / h; t<sub>layer</sub> = L<sub>layer</sub> / v; N = H / z; T<sub>scan</sub> = N t<sub>layer</sub>
blocks.where: A<sub>layer</sub> is scanned area per layer in mm²; h is hatch spacing in mm; L<sub>layer</sub> is scan length per layer in mm; v is scan speed in mm/s; t<sub>layer</sub> is scan time per layer in s; H is part height in mm; z is layer thickness in mm; N is number of layers; T<sub>scan</sub> is total scan time in s.

blocks.text: SLS uses a laser to fuse polymer powder by partial melting. Particle surfaces soften and bond; the centre may stay solid. SLM and DMLS use a laser to fully melt metal powder into dense parts. EBM uses an electron beam in vacuum and a hot powder bed. All are powder bed fusion. Some syllabi call the laser metal version laser powder bed fusion. Laser machines use argon or nitrogen; EBM uses vacuum. The same CAD slice drives every variant; only the energy source and powder change.

items: SLS: nylon and other polymers; good for brackets, ducts and visual models.
SLM/DMLS: steel, aluminium, titanium and cobalt alloys; good for dense functional metal parts.
EBM: titanium and other reactive metals; hot build reduces residual stress but needs vacuum.
Unfused powder supports overhangs in SLS; metal parts still need anchors for heat flow and warping.

blocks.text: Powder quality controls part quality. Particles are tens of micrometres across. Moisture, oxygen and contamination change flow and fusion. Used powder is sieved and blended with fresh powder after checks. Reactive powders such as titanium and aluminium need inert gas and careful housekeeping because fine powder can burn or explode. Laser PBF builds in an argon or nitrogen atmosphere; EBM builds in vacuum. After the build, an unpacking station removes loose powder safely. Metal parts may need CNC machining on mating faces because as-built surfaces are rough. The build direction sets surface finish and anisotropy. Oxygen pick-up lowers ductility. A sieve check and a flow test are routine. Fine powder also needs grounded equipment.

items: Thermal stress: steep heating and cooling cause warping and cracks; use supports, preheat and scan strategy.
Post-processing: depowder, stress relief, support removal, machining, polishing or heat treatment.
Cost: powder handling and post-processing often exceed scan time in a real production plan.

examples.question: A PBF part has layer area 5,000 mm², hatch spacing 0.1 mm, scan speed 800 mm/s, layer thickness 0.05 mm and part height 20 mm. Estimate the laser scan time, ignoring recoating and beam jumps.
steps: Scan length per layer: L = A / h = 5,000 / 0.1 = 50,000 mm.
Time per layer: t = L / v = 50,000 / 800 = 62.5 s.
Number of layers: N = H / z = 20 / 0.05 = 400.
Total scan time: T = N × t = 400 × 62.5 = 25,000 s.
examples.answer: The estimated laser scan time is 25,000 s, about 6.94 h; real build time is higher because recoating adds time.
examples.check:
area = 5000.0
hatch = 0.1
speed = 800.0
layer = 0.05
height = 20.0
scan_length = area / hatch
time_layer = scan_length / speed
layers = height / layer
scan_time = layers * time_layer
scan_hours = scan_time / 3600.0
print(scan_length)
print(time_layer)
print(layers)
print(scan_time)
print(round(scan_hours, 2))

traps: Unfused powder supports overhangs in SLS. In SLM, metal overhangs still need anchors because heat must flow away and warping must be controlled.
SLS is not SLM. SLS sinters polymer powder by partial melting; SLM fully melts metal powder.
Use hatch spacing in the scan-length formula, not layer thickness. Area divided by hatch spacing gives scan length; layer thickness gives the number of layers.
Powder bed fusion is not binder jetting. Binder jetting glues powder with a liquid binder and does not use a laser or electron beam to fuse each slice.
EBM uses an electron beam in vacuum, not a laser. Do not label it as a laser process.

quiz.a: SLS is selective laser sintering; SLM is selective laser melting.

quiz.q: State two functions of the recoater in powder bed fusion.
quiz.a: It spreads a uniform powder layer across the build platform and removes or pushes excess powder away.

quiz.q: Why does SLS not need a separate support under every overhang?
quiz.a: The unfused powder in the bed supports the fused layer. The loose powder is removed after the build.

quiz.q: Give the main difference between SLS and SLM in fusion state and powder.
quiz.a: SLS uses polymer powder and partial melting; SLM uses metal powder and full melting.

quiz.q: A layer area is 2,400 mm², hatch spacing 0.12 mm and scan speed 600 mm/s. Find scan length per layer and scan time per layer.
A metal PBF part warps and cracks near a large overhang during the build. Give two process changes.
quiz.a: Add support anchors for heat flow, preheat the platform or powder, rotate the part to reduce the overhang, or change the scan strategy to spread heat.

quiz.q: Why is powder reuse not simply pouring used powder back into the machine? Name two checks.
quiz.a: Used powder changes in size, shape, moisture and oxygen content. Sieve it, check flow and moisture, check contamination, and blend with fresh powder.

beyond: Not for the exam. Industrial metal PBF now uses multi-laser machines and closed powder-handling stations to raise build rate and reduce operator exposure. Research focuses on scan strategy, melt-pool monitoring and residual-stress prediction. Search terms: laser powder bed fusion, melt pool monitoring, powder reuse, support-free overhangs.
